memory_update.text: Primary direct candidates for the food-input/menu-flexibility node are SYY, USFD, PFGC, SBUX, and TXRH.
For this node, distributors represent procurement-scale and pass-through exposure, while operators like SBUX and TXRH represent direct margin sensitivity to coffee and beef, respectively.

CMG, CAVA, WING, BROS, LKNCY, DRI, YUM, MCD, QSR, DPZ, WEN, SHAK, BLMN, DRI, CAKE, EAT, SGYA, and packaged/protein suppliers such as TSN, HRL, PPC, JBSAY, CALM, LANC, and SJM remain candidates for later passes, but were excluded here to keep the universe to five direct/obvious names.
Need a later supplier-focused pass for protein processors, coffee roasters/packaged coffee companies, dairy, packaging, and restaurant procurement/software/data vendors.

Beef and coffee are currently the clearest commodity watchpoints for this node based on USDA ERS, BLS CPI, and ICO evidence; chicken, dairy, produce, avocado, packaging, and tariffs should be tracked as secondary variables.

node: Food inputs, protein exposure, coffee costs, procurement, and menu flexibility
summary: Expanded the Layer 1B universe around the input-cost chokepoint for restaurants. The most direct public-market mappings are broadline foodservice distributors with purchasing scale and inflation pass-through exposure, plus restaurant operators with concentrated commodity exposure. Current evidence points to beef and coffee as high-signal input categories: USDA/BLS data show food-away-from-home inflation and beef pressure remain relevant in 2026, while ICO data indicate coffee prices remain elevated versus normal historical levels. This pass intentionally limits the universe to five obvious/direct candidates and does not make investment recommendations.
